record.title: The EPPA–Ramsey expansion conjecture
record.statement:
A class of finite structures has **EPPA** if every structure in the class has a finite EPPA-witness, meaning a finite structure into which it embeds such that every partial automorphism extends to an automorphism. An expansion is **precompact** if each structure has only finitely many expansions, up to isomorphism, in the expanded language. A class has the Ramsey property when every finite structure and every number of colors admit a larger structure whose copies of the given structure are monochromatic under every coloring of those copies.

**EPPA–Ramsey expansion conjecture.** Every class with EPPA has a precompact Ramsey expansion.

This conjecture proposes a general connection between the extension property for partial automorphisms and structural Ramsey theory. The paper presents it as a motivating conjecture for the classification of EPPA classes; examples such as finite groups and finite skew-symmetric structures are mentioned as cases where the existence of a precompact Ramsey expansion remains open.
record.source_name: Jan Hubička, Matěj Konečný and Jaroslav Nešetřil, “All those EPPA classes (Strengthenings of the Herwig-Lascar theorem)”, arXiv:1902.03855 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03855

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2019). “See, for example for a definition of a precompact expansion.) Classes known to have EPPA where the existence of a precompact Ramsey expansion is open include the class of all finite groups and the class of all finite skew-symmetr”

record.title: The sparse hypergraph extremal-function conjecture
record.statement:
For fixed integers $r>k\ge 2$ and $e\ge 3$, let $f_r(n,v,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices in which the union of any $e$ distinct edges contains at least $v+1$ vertices. In particular, $f_r(n,e(r-k)+k+1,e)$ concerns the corresponding sparse hypergraphs.

**Sparse hypergraph extremal-function conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
n^{k-o(1)}<f_r(n,e(r-k)+k+1,e)=o(n^k).
$$

The standard bounds give only $\Omega(n^{k-1/(e-1)})\le f_r(n,e(r-k)+k+1,e)=O(n^k)$, so the conjecture predicts a substantially sharper lower bound while asserting that the order remains strictly below $n^k$. The source states that this problem remains widely open.
record.source_name: Chong Shangguan and Itzhak Tamo, “Sparse Hypergraphs with Applications to Coding Theory”, arXiv:1902.05903 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.05903

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

record.title: Schleimer's bounded translation distance conjecture for fibered knots
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold, and let $K\subset M$ be a fibered knot with monodromy acting on the arc complex of its fiber. The translation distance is the minimum distance between an arc and its image under the monodromy.

**Schleimer's conjecture.** There is a constant $t(M)$ such that the monodromy of every fibered knot $K\subset M$ has translation distance in the arc complex of the fiber at most $t(M)$. Furthermore,

$$
t(S^3)=2.
$$

The conjecture predicts a uniform bound depending only on the ambient closed $3$-manifold, with the sharp proposed value for $S^3$. The paper notes that the restriction to knots, rather than links, is essential, and proves that infinitely many fibered Montesinos knots satisfy the asserted $S^3$ bound.
record.source_name: Alexander Stas, “Translation distance bounds for fibered 3-manifolds with boundary”, arXiv:1902.06388 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

record.title: Arman–Gunderson–Tsaturian odd-cycle-free extremal conjecture
record.statement: Let $k>1$ and let $T_2(n)$ be the Turán graph, the complete bipartite graph with its two vertex classes as equal in size as possible. For a graph $G$, write $m(n;C_{2k+1})$ for the maximum number of cycles in an $n$-vertex graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to the odd cycle $C_{2k+1}$. **Arman–Gunderson–Tsaturian conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$, $T_2(n)$ is the unique $n$-vertex $C_{2k+1}$-free graph containing $m(n;C_{2k+1})$ cycles. The paper's main theorem resolves this conjecture for sufficiently large $n$ in the relevant setting, so the conjecture is no longer open.
record.source_name: Natasha Morrison, Alexander Roberts and Alex Scott, “Maximising the Number of Cycles in Graphs with Forbidden Subgraphs”, arXiv:1902.08133 (2020).

record.title: Havet and Yu's $(p,1)$-total labelling conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected graph, let $p$ be a positive integer, and let $\lambda^T_p(G)$ denote the minimum $k$ for which $G$ has a $(p,1)$-total $k$-labelling. **Havet and Yu's conjecture.**

$$
\lambda^T_p(G)\leq \min\\{\Delta(G)+2p-1,2\Delta(G)+p-1\\}.
$$

For $p=1$, this is equivalent to the Total Coloring Conjecture, namely $\chi”(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2$. The source presents the conjecture as open, while noting that substantial special cases are known.
record.source_name: Xin Zhang, Bei Niu and Jiguo Yu, “A structure of 1-planar graph and its applications to coloring problems”, arXiv:1902.08945 (2019).

record.title: The interpolation conjecture for maximal determinants of matrices with non-integer row weight
record.statement:
Let $T(n,\tilde{k})$ be the family of matrices with real row-weight parameter $\tilde{k}>1$, and let $M_T(n,\tilde{k})$ be its maximum determinant. Define

$$
k=\lfloor\tilde{k}\rfloor,\qquad \gamma=\tilde{k}-k,
$$

and

$$
m_1=(1-\gamma)n,\qquad m_2=\gamma n.
$$

Let $M_R(m,n,k)$ denote the corresponding maximum for the family $R(m,n,k)$. **Interpolation conjecture.**

$$
M_T(n,\tilde{k})\le M_R(m_k,n,k)^{1-\gamma}M_R(m_{k+1},n,k+1)^{\gamma}.
$$

The conjecture formalizes the expectation that matrices with non-integer row-weight parameter are controlled by the neighboring integer weights in the appropriate proportions. The source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Daniel Scheinerman, “Maximal determinants of sparse zero-one matrices”, arXiv:1902.09644 (2019).

record.title: Extremal-monomial test-configuration conjecture for isolated hypersurface singularities
record.statement:
Let $f(z_0,z_1,z_2,z_3)$ be an isolated hypersurface singularity. The **extremal monomials** are the monomials selected from the four sets $I$, $II$, $III$, and $IV$ displayed in the source, one from each set, which determine the coordinate weights. A test configuration is a degeneration generated by a $\mathbb C^*$-action whose central fibre has the required enlarged symmetry. **Extremal-monomial test-configuration conjecture.** It suffices to consider only test configurations that eliminate one of the extremal monomials in $f$.
This conjecture proposes a finite restriction on the test configurations relevant to the stability analysis of isolated hypersurface singularities. The source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.

record.title: Polylogarithmic bound for intersecting regular set systems
record.statement:
Let $\beta(w)$ denote the largest $\kappa$ for which there exists an intersecting $\kappa$-regular $w$-set system. Here a $w$-set system is a family of sets of size at most $w$, and regularity is the regularity notion used in the paper. **Polylogarithmic regular-set-system conjecture.** The quantity $\beta(w)$ satisfies

$$
\beta(w)\le(\log w)^{O(1)}.
$$

This statement is presented as a further discussion and is obtained in the paper conditionally from the weak monotone upper-bound DNF compression conjecture; no unconditional resolution is given.
record.source_name: Shachar Lovett, Noam Solomon and Jiapeng Zhang, “From DNF compression to sunflower theorems via regularity”, arXiv:1903.00580 (2019).

record.title: Digraph conjecture on minimum total distance at fixed outradius
record.statement: Let $n$ and $r$ be two positive integers with $n \ge 2r$ and $r \ge 3$. For a digraph $D$, let $W(D)$ denote the sum of distances over all ordered pairs of vertices, let the outradius be the least radius of an out-ball covering all vertices, and let $D_{n,r,s}$ be the digraph defined in the paper. **Minimum-total-distance digraph conjecture.** For any digraph $D$ of order $n$ with outradius $r$, $W(D) \ge W(D_{n,r,1})$. Equality holds if and only if $D \cong D_{n,r,s}$ for $1 \le s \le \frac{n-2r+2}{2}$. This is proposed as the directed analogue of the Chen–Wu–An conjecture for graphs.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, “Extremal total distance of graphs of given radius”, arXiv:1903.01358 (2019).

record.title: Digraph analogue of Vizing's extremal-size theorem
record.statement: Let $r \ge 3$ and $n \ge 2r$. A biconnected digraph is a digraph with no cutvertex, and $D_{n,r,s}$ denotes the family defined in the paper. **Digraph Vizing conjecture.** The maximum size of biconnected digraphs with order $n$ and outradius $r$ is attained by $D_{n,r,1}$. Furthermore, the extremal digraphs are exactly the ones of the form $D_{n,r,s}$ for some $1 \le s \le \frac{n-2r+2}{2}$. The source presents this as the conjectured directed version of Vizing's result, whose graph counterpart is known.

record.title: Adaptive-radius homology computation conjecture for intersections of balls
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subset R^{n+1}$ be a finite set, let $A>0$, and let $\epsilon(x)$ be a positive $A$-Lipschitz continuous function. For each $x\bin\mathcal{X}$, write $B(x,\epsilon(x))$ for the corresponding ball.

**Adaptive-radius homology computation conjecture.** One can compute the homology of

$$
\cap_{x\in \mathcal{X}}B(x,\epsilon(x))
$$

with $\mathcal{X}^{O(n)}$ operations.

This conjecture proposes that the complexity bound known for unions of equal-radius balls extends to intersections of balls with radii varying according to a positive Lipschitz function. The source gives no resolution or further evidence for the conjecture.
record.source_name: Han Jiadong, “An Adaptive Grid Algorithm for Computing the Homology Group of Semialgebraic Set”, arXiv:1903.02388 (2019).

record.title: Maximum positive and stable steady states in the full ERK network
record.statement: Consider the full ERK network and the same network with $k_{\mathrm{on}}=0$, and let a positive steady state mean a steady state with all relevant concentrations positive; call a steady state **positive stable** when it is both positive and stable. **ERK steady-state conjecture.** For each of these two networks, the maximum number of positive steady states is $3$, and the maximum number of positive stable steady states is $2$. This conjecture concerns the sharpness of the bounds in the table and the stability of the steady states; the surrounding discussion establishes multistationarity for the full network but does not resolve these maxima.

record.title: Conjecture on monotonicity of symplectic Kodaira dimension under unchaining
record.statement:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a symplectic $4$-manifold, and let $(X',\omega')$ be obtained from it by an unchaining operation. Write $\kappa(X)$ and $\kappa(X')$ for their symplectic Kodaira dimensions.

**Unchaining monotonicity conjecture.** If $(X',\omega')$ is obtained from $(X,\omega)$ by unchaining, then

$$
\kappa(X') \leq \kappa(X).
$$

The examples in the paper exhibit this non-increasing behavior, alongside the decrease of the second Betti number under unchaining. Whether symplectic Kodaira dimension is non-increasing under every unchaining operation remains open.
record.source_name: R. Inanc Baykur, Kenta Hayano and Naoyuki Monden, “Unchaining surgery and topology of symplectic 4-manifolds”, arXiv:1903.02906 (2019).

record.title: The extension conjecture for varieties containing affine subspaces
record.statement:
Let $V$ be an algebraic variety in $\mathbb F_q^d$. Suppose that $|V|\sim q^{d-1}$ and that $V$ contains an affine subspace $H$ with $|H|=q^k$. The quantity $R_V^*(2\to r)$ is the extension constant in the estimate

$$
\|(fd\sigma)^{\vee}\|_{\ell^r(\mathbb F_q^d)}\le R_V^*(2\to r)\|f\|_{L^2(V,d\sigma)}.
$$

**The extension conjecture.** One has

$$
R_V^*(2\to r)\lesssim 1\quad\text{if}\quad \frac{2(d-k)}{d-k-1}\le r\le\infty.
$$

This would give the optimal $L^2$ extension range suggested by the necessary conditions arising from the dimension of the largest affine subspace contained in $V$. The source presents this as a conjecture; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Daewoong Cheong, Doowon Koh and Thang Pham, “Extension theorems for Hamming varieties over finite fields”, arXiv:1903.03904 (2019).

record.title: Power-sum equality for orientation posets
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{a}$ be an area sequence of length $n$, let $O(\mathbf{a})$ be the set of orientations associated with $\mathbf{a}$, let $P(\theta)$ be the poset obtained from the ascending edges of $\theta$, and let $B(\theta)$ be the disjoint union of chains whose lengths are given by $\overline{\pi}(\theta)$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $\mathcal{O}^{\ast}_{\lambda}(P)$ denote the set of order-preserving surjections of type $\lambda$ whose fibers have unique minimal elements. **Equivalent power-sum conjecture.** For every area sequence $\mathbf{a}$ of length $n$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash n$,

$$
\sum_{\theta\in O(\mathbf{a})}q^{\operatorname{asc}(\theta)}\left|\mathcal{O}^{\ast}_{\lambda}(P(\theta))\right|=\sum_{\theta\in O(\mathbf{a})}q^{\operatorname{asc}(\theta)}\left|\mathcal{O}^{\ast}_{\lambda}(B(\theta))\right|.
$$

This is stated as an equivalent reformulation of the main LLT identity after comparing power-sum coefficients; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Per Alexandersson, “LLT polynomials, elementary symmetric functions and melting lollipops”, arXiv:1903.03998 (2019).

record.title: Spectrally reasonable measures conjecture for locally compact Abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact non-discrete Abelian group. Write $4\mathcal{S}(G)4$ for the spectrally reasonable measures on $G$, $\mathcal{M}_{00}(G)$ for the measures with Rajchman-type vanishing Fourier–Stieltjes transform, and $\operatorname{lin}(\delta_0)$ for the linear span of the point mass at the identity. 

**Spectrally reasonable measures conjecture.**

$$
\begin{cases}
\mathcal{S}(G)=\mathcal{M}_{00}(G)\oplus\operatorname{lin}(\delta_0), & \text{if }G\text{ is compact},\\
\mathcal{S}(G)=\operatorname{lin}(\delta_0), & \text{if }G\text{ is non-compact}.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture proposes a complete description of spectrally reasonable measures for all locally compact non-discrete Abelian groups. The surrounding discussion notes that the compact case is supported by the results proved earlier, while the argument does not extend directly to all compact groups, including groups of $p$-adic integers; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Przemysław Ohrysko and Michał Wojciechowski, “Spectrally reasonable measures II”, arXiv:1903.04853 (2019).

record.title: Effective-bound conjecture for incidence strata
record.statement:
For fixed $k\geq 1$, let $N_k(P)$ be the minimum integer $n$ such that $\Delta^k_P$ embeds into $\mathbb{A}^n$, and let $N_k$ denote the upper bound in the displayed chain

$$
\max \{N_k(P)\mid P \in \mathbb{N}^k\}\le \max \{N_k(P)\mid P \in (\mathbb{C}^k)^{\circ}\}\le N_k.
$$

**Effective-bound conjecture.** These three quantities equal $2^k-1$ for $k\geq 1$.
This conjecture gives the expected sharp value of the embedding dimension bound for the incidence strata, while the source does not provide a resolution of it.
record.source_name: Hunter Spink and Dennis Tseng, “Incidence strata of affine varieties with complex multiplicities”, arXiv:1903.05011 (2019).

record.title: The non-Frobenius o-monomial stabilizer conjecture
record.statement:
Let $q=2^m$, let $x^e$ be an o-monomial over ${\mathrm{GF}}(q)$, and let $J_e$ be the associated subset used in the design construction. Write ${\mathrm{AG}}_1({\mathrm{GF}}(q))$ for the affine group of degree one and ${\mathrm{Stab}}_{{\mathrm{AG}}_1({\mathrm{GF}}(q))}(J_e)$ for the subgroup stabilizing $J_e$. **The non-Frobenius o-monomial stabilizer conjecture.** If $e$ is not a power of $2$, then

$$
{\mathrm{Stab}}_{{\mathrm{AG}}_1({\mathrm{GF}}(q))}(J_e)=\{x\}.
$$

Consequently, the design ${\mathbb{D}}(x^e,q/2)$ has parameters $3$-$(q,q/2,q(q-4)/8)$. Experimental data strongly supports this conjecture; the stated stabilizer condition would determine the parameters of the resulting $3$-design.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding and Chunming Tang, “Combinatorial t-designs from special polynomials”, arXiv:1903.07375 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07375

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2019). “The following is a fundamental open problem.”

record.title: ML degree formula for the MA(1) model
record.statement:
Let $MA(1)$ be the moving-average model with $n>1$ sample points, and let its maximum-likelihood degree be the number of complex critical points of the likelihood function for generic data. **ML degree conjecture.** The ML degree of $MA(1)$ for $n>1$ sample points is equal to

$$
4(n-1).
$$

The formula is inferred from ML degree computations for $n=2,3,\dots$; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution, so the general claim remains open.
record.source_name: Carlos Améndola and Viet Son Pham, “Autocovariance Varieties of Moving Average Random Fields”, arXiv:1903.08611 (2019).

record.title: Characterization conjecture for forcing number and parallel paths
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $3$, let $n$ be the number of vertices of $G$, and let $F(G)$ denote its forcing number. A **$k$-parallel path graph** is a graph of $k$-parallel paths. **Parallel-path characterization conjecture.** For some $k\in[n]$,

$$
F(G)=k \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is a graph of }k\text{-parallel paths}.
$$

The conjecture seeks to characterize all forcing numbers of graphs of maximum degree at most three by the number of parallel paths. The source says it is supported by earlier results and observations, but gives no resolution status.

record.title: Unbounded ratio of maximum throttling number to maximum cop number
record.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $mc(n)$ and $mt(n)$ denote, respectively, the maximum cop number and maximum cop throttling number over all connected graphs of order $n$. **The unbounded-ratio conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{mt(n)}{mc(n)}=\infty.
$$

The claim predicts that maximum cop throttling can grow arbitrarily faster than maximum cop number. The surrounding discussion introduces this as a further question after establishing bounds on cop throttling, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: Černý–Starke conjecture on synchronizing automata
record.statement:
A synchronizing automaton is a finite automaton whose transition semigroup contains a word sending every state to the same state; its reset threshold $rt(\mathcal{A})$ is the length of a shortest such synchronizing word. **The Černý–Starke conjecture.** Any synchronizing automaton on $n$ states has a synchronizing word of length at most

$$
(n-1)^2.
$$

This is a longstanding open problem in automata theory concerning the maximum reset threshold of synchronizing automata.
record.source_name: Costanza Catalano, Umer Azfar, Ludovic Charlier and Raphaël Jungers, “A linear bound on the k-rendezvous time for primitive sets of NZ matrices”, arXiv:1903.10421 (2021).

record.title: The Frobenius structure conjecture: weak Gromov–Witten version
record.statement:
Let $(Y,D)$ be a Fano pair. Let $B(\mathbb{Z})$ denote the integral tropical points, with corresponding generators $\vartheta_q$ of $\operatorname{QH}_{\log}^0(Y,D)$, and let $\langle\cdot\rangle$ be the multilinear point function defined from the logarithmic Gromov–Witten numbers.

**Weak Gromov–Witten Frobenius structure conjecture.** There exists a product $*$ on $\operatorname{QH}_{\log}^0(Y,D)$ making it a commutative associative $\mathbb{Q}[\operatorname{NE}(Y)]$-algebra with identity $\vartheta_{[Y]}$ such that

$$
\langle \vartheta_{q_1},\ldots,\vartheta_{q_s}\rangle=\langle\vartheta_{q_1}*\cdots*\vartheta_{q_s}\rangle
$$

for all $s$-tuples $q_1,\ldots,q_s\in B(\mathbb{Z})$ with $s\geq1$.

This conjecture asserts that the logarithmic Gromov–Witten point functions of every Fano pair arise from a single associative commutative product. The parser supplies no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Travis Mandel, “Fano mirror periods from the Frobenius structure conjecture”, arXiv:1903.12014 (2019).

record.title: Fractional Erdős matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f_0^s(\ell,m)$ be the smallest integer $m'$ such that every $m$-vertex $ell$-uniform hypergraph with minimum $0$-degree at least $m'$ has a fractional matching of size $s$, and set $s=(m+d)/(\ell+d)$.

**Fractional Erdős matching conjecture.** For integers $\ell,d\geq1$,

$$
\limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac{f_0^s(\ell,m)}{\binom{m}{\ell}}\leq1-\left(1-\frac{1}{\ell+d}\right)^\ell.
$$

This is described as a fractional version of the Erdős matching conjecture and as sufficient, via a reduction, to establish the fractional perfect matching threshold conjecture. The supplied text gives partial cases but does not state a complete resolution.
record.source_name: Asaf Ferber and Vishesh Jain, “Uniformity-independent minimum degree conditions for perfect matchings in hypergraphs”, arXiv:1903.12207 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1107.1219](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1219).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.12207

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2019). “On the other hand, for $d<k/2$, has been verified for only a few cases (see the discussion in ) and, for example, even the case $d=1$ and $k=6$ is open.”

record.title: Babu–Diwan-type subdivision conjecture for vertex-disjoint even cycles
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph of order $n$ with $k$ components, each of which is an even cycle. Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with bipartition $(X,Y)$ such that

$$
|X|=|Y|\geq n/2.
$$

**Subdivision conjecture.** If the minimum degree of $G$ is at least $n/2-k+1$, then $G$ contains a subdivision of $H$.

This conjecture extends the preceding theorem, which proves the same assertion when every cycle has length at least $6$, and includes the vertex-disjoint-cycle result as a special case. The statement concerns the degree threshold guaranteeing subdivisions of graphs whose components are even cycles.
record.source_name: Shengning Qiao and Bing Chen, “Subdivisions of vertex-disjoint cycles in bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1904.01794 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01794

record.title: Burcroff's irredundance conjecture for direct products of balanced complete multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=\prod_{i=1}^n K[u_i,t_i]$ be a direct product of balanced complete multipartite graphs. The independence number $\alpha(G)$ is the largest size of an independent set, and $\operatorname{IR}(G)$ is the maximum size of an irredundant set. **Burcroff's conjecture.**

$$
\alpha(G)=\operatorname{IR}(G).
$$

This strengthens the earlier conjecture that the independence number equals the upper domination number for these products. The conjecture is known in the cases $t_n\leq 2$ and $n\leq 3$, but the source does not establish its general resolution.
record.source_name: Noga Alon and Colin Defant, “Isoperimetry, Stability, and Irredundance in Direct Products”, arXiv:1904.02595 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.02595

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The irredundance conjecture for direct products of complete multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ be complete multipartite graphs, and let $G=\prod_{i=1}^n H_i$. The independence number $\alpha(G)$ is the largest size of an independent set, and $\operatorname{IR}(G)$ is the maximum size of an irredundant set. **Irredundance conjecture.**

$$
\alpha(G)=\operatorname{IR}(G).
$$

This removes the assumption that the factors are balanced and is presented as a strengthening of Burcroff's conjecture. The source does not provide a resolution of this broader statement.

record.title: The normal 5-edge-coloring conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **normal edge-coloring** is a proper edge-coloring in which every edge $uv$ satisfies $|S_c(u)\cup S_c(v)|\in\{3,5\}$, where $S_c(v)$ is the set of colors on the edges incident with $v$. Let $\chi'_N(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a normal edge-coloring of $G$. **Normal 5-edge-coloring conjecture.** For any bridgeless cubic graph $G$, $\chi'_N(G)\leq 5$. By Jaeger's equivalence, this is a reformulation of the Petersen coloring conjecture and remains open in general.
record.source_name: Luca Ferrarini, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Normal 5-edge-colorings of a family of Loupekhine snarks”, arXiv:1904.02661 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.02661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Körner's reversing permutations conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Two permutations of $[n]$ are **reversing** if, viewed as vectors of length $n$, two coordinates contain the same two elements $\{a,b\}\subset[n]$ in reversed order. Let $RP(n)$ be the maximum size of a pairwise reversing family of permutations of $[n]$. **Körner's conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
RP(n)\leq C^n.
$$

This conjecture is the main motivation for studying Hamiltonian paths that create even cycles. The source also gives equivalent formulations in terms of pairwise $C_4$-creating perfect matchings and homomorphism counts, but does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Gergely Harcos and Daniel Soltész, “New bounds on even cycle creating Hamiltonian paths using expander graphs”, arXiv:1904.04601 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04601

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Quantum A-polynomial conjecture for knot series
record.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot, let $\Delta_K(x)$ be its Alexander polynomial, and let $f_K(x,q)$ be the normalized knot series. Let $\widehat{A}$ denote the quantum A-polynomial, acting as a $q$-difference operator in $x$.

**Quantum A-polynomial conjecture.** For any knot $K\subset S^3$,

$$
\widehat{A}f_K(x,q)=0.
$$

Furthermore,

$$
\lim_{q\to1}f_K(x,q)=\operatorname{s.e.}\left(\frac{1}{\Delta_K(x)}\right),
$$

where $\operatorname{s.e.}$ is the average of the expansions of the rational function at $x\to0$ and $x\to\infty$. This supplies a boundary value for the recursion and is intended to determine the series together with the quantum A-polynomial equation.
record.source_name: Sergei Gukov and Ciprian Manolescu, “A two-variable series for knot complements”, arXiv:1904.06057 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06057

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2019). “Mathematically, it was proved that the colored Jones function is $q$-holonomic, that is, it satisfies a finite linear recursion with polynomial coefficients .”

record.title: Minimum dominator chromatic number of orientations of generalized stars
record.statement:
Let $GS_{m}^{k}$ be a generalized star, and let $\chi_{d}(GS_{m}^{k})$ denote its dominator chromatic number. **The generalized-star minimum conjecture.** The minimum dominator chromatic number over all orientations of $GS_{m}^{k}$ is given by

$$
\chi_{d}(GS_{m}^{k})=3+m\left(\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor-1\right).
$$

The paper establishes an upper bound and conjectures that this bound is best possible; the status of the claimed minimum is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: Michael Cary, “Dominator Chromatic Numbers of Orientations of Trees”, arXiv:1904.06293 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Maximum dominator chromatic number of orientations of generalized stars
record.statement:
Let $GS_{m}^{k}$ be a generalized star, and let $\chi_{d}(GS_{m}^{k})$ denote its dominator chromatic number. An **(anti-)arborescence** is an orientation of the generalized star that is an arborescence or an anti-arborescence. **The generalized-star maximum conjecture.** The maximum dominator chromatic number over all orientations of $GS_{m}^{k}$ is

$$
m(k-1)+2,
$$

and this maximum occurs when $GS_{m}^{k}$ is an (anti-)arborescence. The paper describes these orientations as conjecturally worst possible, but gives no resolution of the claim.
record.source_name: Michael Cary, “Dominator Chromatic Numbers of Orientations of Trees”, arXiv:1904.06293 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Bounded-constant conjecture for small values of bounded-spectrum functions
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a trigonometric polynomial with $n+1$ terms, and let $H_f$ denote the maximum modulus of its nonconstant coefficients. Write $J_f(u)$ for the measure of the set where $|f|<u$, and let $C_n$ be the constants in the previously established estimate

$$
J_f(u)\leq C_n H_f^{1/n}u^{1/n}.
$$

**Bounded-constant conjecture.** In the estimate above, $C_n$ can be replaced by a bounded sequence.

The claim would substantially improve the quantitative small-value estimates proved in the paper, whose constants are currently obtained recursively and are only known from computation to have a bounded normalized limit. Its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Wayne Lawton, “Distribution of Small Values of Bohr Almost Periodic Functions with Bounded Spectrum”, arXiv:1904.09373 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.09373

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: The conjecture that satellite knots are not quasi-alternating
record.statement:
Let a **satellite knot** be a knot whose exterior contains an incompressible torus. Let $\mathcal{Q}$ denote the class of quasi-alternating links, defined as the smallest set containing the unknot and closed under the crossing-smoothing recursion with determinant additivity. **Satellite knots are not quasi-alternating.**

This conjecture extends the known fact that prime alternating knots are not satellite knots in the context of quasi-alternating knots. Gordon and Lidman proved that cable knots have double branched covers that are not $L$-spaces, so cable knots are not quasi-alternating; the conjecture remains open for satellite knots in general.
record.source_name: Subhankar Dey, “Cable knots are not thin”, arXiv:1904.11591 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.11591

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: The three-cover multiplicity conjecture for hypercubes
record.statement:
Let $Q^n=\{0,1\}^n$ be the vertex set of the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $g(n,m,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices covered fewer than $k$ times by $m$ affine hyperplanes not passing through $\vec{0}$. For $n\geq m\geq 1$, the conjecture concerns the range $1\leq m\leq n+3$.

**Three-cover multiplicity conjecture.**

$$
g(n,m,3)=
 \begin{cases}
 2^n, & m=1,2;\\
 2^{n-1}, & m=3;\\
 2^{n-m+3}, & m=4,\ldots,n+3.
 \end{cases}
$$

The first two cases and the stated lower and upper bounds motivate the conjecture; the paper does not report a proof of the full piecewise formula, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Alexander Clifton and Hao Huang, “On almost k-covers of hypercubes”, arXiv:1904.12885 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12885

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Genericity of Assumption (J2)
record.statement: Let $F(\mathbf{z})=G(\mathbf{z})/H(\mathbf{z})$ be a rational function, and let Assumption (J2) denote the Jacobian nondegeneracy condition used in the paper's critical-point system. **Genericity conjecture.** Assumption (J2) holds generically. This is used to ensure that the relevant polynomial system has finitely many solutions and hence that the algorithm can determine the critical points; the source gives no resolution, so the genericity assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Stephen Melczer and Bruno Salvy, “Effective Coefficient Asymptotics of Multivariate Rational Functions via Semi-Numerical Algorithms for Polynomial Systems”, arXiv:1905.04187 (2020).

record.title: Conjecture on Möbius invariance of O'Hara knot energies
record.statement: For $d4aa^{\alpha,p}$ an O'Hara knot energy with $d4aa^{\alpha,p}$ defined for $d4aa p\geq 4$ and $p\geq 2$, the parameters $d4aa$ and $p$ determine its scaling and invariance properties. **Möbius-invariance conjecture.** The energy $d4aa^{\alpha,p}$ is Möbius invariant if and only if $(\alpha,p)=(2,2)$. This conjecture is supported in the source by strong numerical evidence; the source does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Simon Blatt, Philipp Reiter and Armin Schikorra, “On O'hara knot energies I: Regularity for critical knots”, arXiv:1905.06064 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.06064

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2019). “This conjecture was proven by Hatcher .”

record.title: The Euclidean mechanical systems kernel conjecture
record.statement:
For each dimension $d\geq 1$, let $V\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a smooth potential and let $\Phi_V$ be the homomorphism from the universal Lie algebra of classical mechanics to the Lie algebra generated by the Euclidean kinetic energy $T(p)=\frac{1}{2}p\cdot p$ and $V$ under the canonical Poisson bracket. The universal identities include antisymmetry, the Jacobi identity, and the vanishing of the Lie bracket of two elements of degree $0$.

**Euclidean kernel conjecture.** Consider all smooth potentials $V\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with arbitrary $d$. Then

$$
\bigcap_{d\geq 1}\bigcap_{V\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)}\ker(\Phi_V)=0.
$$

This is the precise formulation of the claim that no relations beyond the inherited universal identities are shared by all smooth Euclidean mechanical systems. The paper presents it as unproved.
record.source_name: Robert I McLachlan and Ander Murua, “The Lie algebra of classical mechanics”, arXiv:1905.07554 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.07554

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

record.title: Dodgson-intersection model conjecture for nonzero $c_2$-invariants
record.statement: A $c_2$-invariant has a minimal model if it is represented by a projective variety of smallest possible dimension, and a Dodgson intersection is the variety defined by an intersection of Dodgson polynomials. **Dodgson-intersection conjecture.** Every non-zero $c_2$ has a minimal model which is a Dodgson intersection. This conjecturally identifies the geometric form underlying every nonzero graph-theoretic $c_2$-invariant, but no general proof is known.
record.source_name: Oliver Schnetz, “Geometries in perturbative quantum field theory”, arXiv:1905.08083 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08083

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2019). “Although the conjecture is false in general , a connection between the point-counting function and the period $()$ remains valid.”

record.title: Conjecture on optimal gaps in cycle spectra of 3-connected cubic planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}(G)$ denote the cycle spectrum of a graph $G$, and let the **circumference** of $G$ be the length of its longest cycle. **Conjecture on optimal gaps.** If $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq 2$ and $G$ is a 3-connected cubic planar graph of circumference at least $k$, then

$$
\mathcal{C}(G)\cap [k,2k+2]\neq\emptyset.
$$

The conjecture would show that the constructions in Section 3 have the largest possible gaps among 3-connected cubic planar graphs. The paper proves the weaker bound with $2k+9$ in place of $2k+2$, while the sharp bound remains open.
record.source_name: Martin Merker, “Gaps in the cycle spectrum of 3-connected cubic planar graphs”, arXiv:1905.09101 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09101

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2019).
